findings.title: Private shelter makes brotherhood operative before public pressure
findings.claim: Joseph's taking his brother into protective nearness and naming their brotherhood turns the consolation into a private act of protection: the brother's grief is addressed inside a relationship that is no longer borne alone, before the surrounding public procedure unfolds.
findings.mechanism: The transitive sheltering form at 12:69:5:1 carries the brother into Joseph's guarded nearness; the two brother forms at 12:69:7:1 and 12:69:11:1 provide the independent relational trigger; the no-grief form at 12:69:13:1 changes that contact into an affective reassurance. Same-surah connections to 12:79 and 12:90 return this focus relation through later retention pressure and public recognition, while the 11:36 connection supplies a separate consolation context for the same no-grief form.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah becomes perceptible as a protected disclosure: kinship is named inside shelter, and reassurance is given before the relationship is exposed to the next public mechanism.
findings.containment: The plain familial reunion and consolation remain intact. This does not claim that the later procedure is grammatically predicted, that the brothers consciously share every wider implication, or that the focus words lose their ordinary meanings.

epistemic.reason: The trusted anchored finding supplies exact focus contacts and branch assignments, while the reader-walk supports and wider connection rows are legacy or target-morphology-limited evidence for the contextual extension.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir varlık, kendisini toplayan veya barındıran bir yere yönelip oraya katılır.
branch_activations.carrier: Joseph's completed act of taking the brother into a place of protective nearness.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 12:79 connection records the later public refusal to substitute another for the retained brother, giving the earlier receiving act a concrete pressure context.
branch_activations.activation: The focus sheltering act contacts the later retention context through the same brother who has been privately received; the relation expands shelter from immediate nearness to protection under public pressure.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The private receiving can be read as protective preparation for the brother's exposure to the next procedure.
branch_activations.boundary: The connection supplies a contextual parallel, not proof that the future procedure is encoded in the shelter verb.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Başkasını bir yere alıp yerleştirme ve barındırma aynı çekirdeğin ettirgen görünümüdür.
branch_activations.carrier: The transitive form presents Joseph as the one who actively places and shelters another person.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The later same-surah connection identifies a public custody pressure in which Benjamin remains the singled-out person.
branch_activations.activation: The active sheltering carrier meets the later custody trigger and makes Joseph's nearness function as a protective enclosure rather than mere location.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Joseph's reception of the brother carries the added effect of shielding him before the public mechanism can be read from the outside.
branch_activations.boundary: This retains the ordinary barındırma sense and does not assert that the act legally guarantees the later outcome.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel alan, erkek ve kadın kardeşleri ve aralarındaki doğum ya da soy bağını kapsar.
branch_activations.carrier: The two sibling forms name a concrete brotherhood first in the sheltered address and then in Joseph's explicit self-identification.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 12:90 connection records this private disclosure becoming public recognition.
branch_activations.activation: The focus kinship carrier meets the later public-recognition trigger, so the private naming becomes the first protected stage of a restored identity that can later be disclosed openly.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Brotherhood is not only stated as a fact; it becomes a relation that moves from hidden mutual knowledge toward public restoration.
branch_activations.boundary: The later connection supports resonance and sequence, not a claim that the focus clause itself narrates 12:90.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişiye karşı acıma, iç yumuşaması ve üzülme duygusu dalın çekirdeğidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The receiving act turns Joseph toward the brother as a person brought into his immediate care.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The following no-grief address explicitly responds to the brother's distress and the harm attributed to the others.
branch_activations.activation: The sheltering carrier contacts the affective trigger in the same focus sentence, allowing physical receiving and inward softening to describe one protective movement without merging their lexical branches.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The act of sheltering carries a compassionate orientation toward the brother as well as a spatial reception.
branch_activations.boundary: The shelter verb is not redefined as compassion; the affective reading arises from its contact with the addressed consolation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Hoşlanılmayan bir durumun kişide üzüntü ve iç rahatsızlığı doğurması anlatılır.
branch_activations.carrier: The negative imperative addresses the brother's possible grief, inner disturbance, and complaint over what the others have done.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 11:36 connection contains the same consolation formula in a distinct context.
branch_activations.activation: The separate consolation context returns through the exact focus form and confirms that the clause can function as speech that interrupts grief without removing the surrounding harm.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The brother is invited to remain within the newly named relationship rather than be defined by the sorrow caused by the others.
branch_activations.boundary: The parallel establishes a consolation function, not identical circumstances or a replacement for the focus's ordinary past-action reference.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Olumsuz kalıpta kişiye üzülmemesi, yakınmaması ve bu sıkıntıya saplanmaması söylenir.
branch_activations.carrier: The negative form directly tells the addressed brother not to remain sunk in grief or complaint.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The exact-form connection to 11:36 supplies an independent consoling use of the same expression.
branch_activations.activation: The focus carrier and the separate consolation trigger meet in the speech act, making the reassurance a bounded response to harm rather than a denial that harm occurred.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The newly restored bond gives the brother a place from which the earlier injury can be endured without solitary despair.
branch_activations.boundary: No claim is made that the later context controls the focus meaning or that the form carries a universal therapeutic promise.

findings.title: Private recognition becomes public restoration
findings.claim: The focus's private naming of brotherhood can be perceived as the first concealed stage of a later public restoration of identity.
findings.mechanism: The brotherhood carrier at 12:69:11:1 names the relation inside private shelter; the supplied 12:90 connection is an independent later trigger that records public recognition; the focus return remains the explicit brother predicate rather than the whole ayah.
findings.reader_payoff: The brief self-identification acquires a longer relational arc: what is known between two people can later become speakable before the wider family.
findings.containment: This is a qualified same-surah resonance, not a claim that 12:69 grammatically forecasts 12:90 or that private knowledge is already public in the focus scene.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective support and the connection row supply the concrete later coordinate, but the reader source is legacy-unbound and the target's morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel alan, erkek ve kadın kardeşleri ve aralarındaki doğum ya da soy bağını kapsar.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The brotherhood named in the room can later cross the boundary into public acknowledgment.
branch_activations.boundary: The connection supports a relational sequence, not an assertion that the focus scene itself includes public recognition.

findings.title: Private shelter expands toward family safety
findings.claim: Joseph's act of taking his brother into shelter can resonate as the private beginning of a protection that later extends to the parents and the settled safety of the family.
findings.mechanism: The transitive shelter carrier at 12:69:5:1 meets the independent 12:99 connection, whose supplied target repeats Joseph's receiving action with his parents and invites entry in safety; the focus return stays on the sheltering word.
findings.reader_payoff: The immediate embrace becomes a small-scale form of a later family settlement, so protection is seen moving from one endangered relation toward a wider homecoming.
findings.containment: The parallel does not make the brother and parents interchangeable, does not claim intentional foreshadowing, and does not replace the focus's immediate private scene with the later settlement.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective and connection identify an exact later sheltering act, but the reader source is legacy-unbound and the target morphology is not supplied.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The private shelter can be seen as the first local instance of a protection that later becomes family-wide settlement.

branch_activations.boundary: The shared sheltering pattern does not erase the distinct narrative circumstances or establish direct causal prediction.
